A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIP research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning and tool-augmented-reasoning experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, assumption tests, and training trajectories.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and supplementary analyses, with revised numerical results and new reward and advantage trajectories.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the GP prediction/update procedure, continuous rollout allocation, and greedy rounding. The continuous-reward extension is also retained. The changed theoretical gradient scalar does not change the documented allocation rule, which assumes a common gradient-factor variance across prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DAPO-MATH-17k and MuSiQue and evaluate on AIME2024, AIME2025, Bamboogle, and MuSiQue. The revised training trajectories and diagnostics reuse this coverage without introducing new tasks or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix F removes the RLOO versus RLOO+VIP trajectory comparison and retains only GRPO versus GRPO+VIP. The main Dr. GRPO/RLOO comparisons, allocation-heuristic ablations, and Moving Average/Ridge Regression predictor comparisons retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes the stated training duration from one to two epochs and budgets from {6Q, 8Q} to {8Q, 16Q}; Table 1 relabels its lower block accordingly. Appendix F changes from one epoch at 512×8 rollouts per batch to two epochs at 512×8 or 512×16. These are substantive reported protocol revisions, although Table 9 still lists 6/8/Dynamic responses and the PDFs do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix F replaces the explicit GRPO/RLOO seed-stability study with GRPO-only training dynamics at two budgets, adding mean-advantage and mean-reward diagnostics. Appendix B also removes projection-based assumption-test results from Tables 5, 6, and 8 while retaining their norm-based counterparts; Table 7 retains both. The component ablations and predictor-error analysis remain.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports five random seeds and means with standard deviations for Appendix F, with shaded uncertainty bands in Figures 6–7. v3 removes the seed count, standard-deviation description, and bands, showing curves labeled as means without replacement uncertainty information. This establishes reduced reporting, not necessarily fewer experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B Dr. GRPO and Dr. GRPO+VIP values in both budget blocks. For example, upper-block AIME24 Pass@32 changes from 18.29/25.0 to 34.56/33.63, reversing their ranking; changed epoch settings prevent interpreting this as a matched performance gain. Appendix F replaces trajectories and adds reward/advantage results, while Tables 5, 6, and 8 delete projection-based p-values. Tables 2–4 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Section 4 redefines Z from the linear projection 1^T H to ||H||_2, changing G into an advantage-weighted sum of norms and changing the quantity covered by the assumptions and variance propositions. This is substantive mathematics, not equivalent notation. Appendix A.1 also restores missing factors of two in the C1 cross-term expansion; the allocation theorems retain their formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: variance analysis motivates GP-based prediction and optimized rollout allocation, improving sampling efficiency and benchmark performance. The revised evidence does not produce a corresponding revision of these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F withdraws claims of consistently faster, smoother, lower-variance training across seeds and instead interprets reward and advantage trajectories as richer learning signals, with superiority at most checkpoints. Section 4 adds a rationale about proxying parameter-update scale. The main benchmark interpretations and applicability discussion otherwise remain.

D1.justification: v1 supplies an anonymized repository URL and describes the named GitHub repository as forthcoming. v3 removes the anonymous URL and prominently labels the named repository as Source Code, changing the advertised access information. Actual repository availability cannot be established from the PDFs; implementation descriptions and Table 9 are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds six references covering DART-Math, DPO, and test-time scaling/search/planning work by Snell, Feng, and Nguyen and colleagues. It adds a short comparison favoring post-training at lower inference budgets. Section 2's positioning against adaptive rollout and data-selection methods remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction receives a localized expansion, Section 3 clarifies the clipped-surrogate terminology, and Section 4 and Appendix F contain revised explanations. Author information and acknowledgments also change. The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The training displays are substantially restructured: separate six-panel GRPO and RLOO figures become a four-panel reward/advantage figure and a twelve-panel GRPO comparison across two budgets, without uncertainty bands. The predictor-error figure moves from the main text to Appendix C, Tables 5, 6, and 8 lose a data column, and the title/author block is reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects a proof expansion and adds training diagnostics, but loses v1's explicit five-seed uncertainty reporting and introduces a budget mismatch between Section 6 and Table 9. Section 4 also describes its new advantage-weighted sum of norms as a gradient norm, although these quantities are not generally equal, while the propositions still refer to projections. These reduce statistical transparency and internal consistency despite retaining the core procedure and broad empirical coverage.
